To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a physics-based simulation model can be learned and used for clothing synthesis, that a model that factors clothing deformation due to body shape and pose can be learned, and that this factorization greatly simplifies clothing animation.
a learned model of clothing can be used to synthesize realistic cloth on bodies of varying shape and pose, and that this approach is significantly more efficient and robust than physical simulation.

a physics-based model of cloth can be learned to approximate the cloth deformation on a body of any shape and that this approximation is accurate and efficient enough to be used for realistic animation of clothed characters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an efficient and robust method for dressing a wide variety of human bodies with realistic clothing.
the problem of dressing synthetic bodies in a way that is realistic, efficient and automated.
the development of a system to automatically generate realistic clothing for virtual characters in a variety of shapes and poses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method is a complete system for synthesizing clothing on bodies of any shape.
DRAPE can dress any person in any garment in a physically plausible way.
the DRAPE model provides an approximation to clothing deformation due to body pose that is accurate for a variety of garments and body shapes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a system for dressing virtual characters that can be used to produce realistic clothing on bodies of any shape.
we have developed the first system for dressing any virtual human body of varying shape with a realistic garment.
we have developed an algorithm for automatically generating clothing that is customized to the body shape, and that is animated to fit the body motion.

we show how to learn an approximation to the physics-based clothing deformation and use it for clothing synthesis.
we can learn an approximation of the cloth dynamics that can be used to generate clothing on bodies of any shape.
a model of clothing learned from a simulation can be used to drive a physically plausible animation of the clothing.
